profiles.meeting_scenario: Outside counsel for a biotech sponsor and in-house counsel at an academic medical center are holding a coordination meeting about the legal review handoff for an investigator-initiated Phase II oncology trial protocol that is being revised using the SPIRIT 2013 Statement and its Explanation and Elaboration paper. The immediate context is that the sponsor wants a near-final protocol for internal governance review, while the site wants to keep the study on track for single-IRB submission and contract drafting. The agenda is to align on which protocol version is being reviewed, what will be included in the shared protocol package, how SPIRIT-based comments will be delivered, and what each side means by the protocol being submission-ready next week. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on timing, deliverables, and ownership of the next handoff between the sponsor legal review and the site submission workstream.

members.name: Elena Park
members.expertise: FDA-regulated clinical trial governance, sponsor-side protocol review, research compliance documentation
members.background: Elena is outside counsel to emerging biopharma companies and routinely reviews interventional trial protocols for consistency with regulatory commitments, operational feasibility language, and sponsor governance expectations before studies move to execution.
members.private_state: She wants to keep the sponsor's governance committee review on schedule and minimize another review cycle by getting a legally sufficient protocol packet that can be circulated internally without reopening settled drafting issues.
hidden_assumptions: When someone says the 'latest draft,' they mean the sponsor master protocol version 3.2 that was circulated in redline to core reviewers on Friday, because the sponsor document control team treats that as the current authoritative version.

A 'protocol package' naturally includes the protocol, synopsis, schedule-of-assessments appendix, and any companion documents needed for sponsor review, but not a separate SPIRIT mapping table unless someone specifically asks for it.

If the team says the protocol will be 'submission-ready,' it means ready for sponsor governance sign-off with placeholders allowed for site-specific administrative details so long as substantive protocol sections are stable.
SPIRIT-based legal comments should be made directly in the Word draft or embedded as tracked changes against the master protocol, because that is how sponsor-side reviewers preserve version lineage.

members.name: Daniel Ruiz
members.role: Associate General Counsel, Research & Clinical Trials
members.expertise: Academic medical center research law, IRB submission coordination, clinical trial agreement interfaces, institutional policy compliance
members.background: Daniel supports investigator-initiated and industry-sponsored studies at a large teaching hospital and regularly coordinates among investigators, the IRB office, budget staff, and outside counsel to get protocol materials into institutionally acceptable form.
members.private_state: He wants to avoid delays to the institution's single-IRB slot and ensure the site team receives a complete packet they can upload with minimal back-and-forth, even if sponsor-facing formatting and version conventions differ.
hidden_assumptions: When someone refers to the 'latest draft,' they mean the latest clean IRB-facing protocol file in the shared site folder, currently version 3.1 clean with the revised participant timeline appendix uploaded Monday.

A 'protocol package' for this handoff includes the protocol, SPIRIT checklist or crosswalk, investigator brochure reference note, and site-facing appendices required for IRB intake, because those items travel together in institutional workflow.

A protocol is 'submission-ready' only when all required sections and attachments for IRB upload are complete, with no blanks and with institutional injury language and contact details inserted where expected.

SPIRIT-related review comments are most usefully captured in the issue tracker keyed to checklist items rather than embedded in the document itself, because that is how the site team assigns and closes comments across departments.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the protocol package
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that Elena will review and return the 'protocol package' before the next handoff.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena understands the protocol package as the protocol draft plus sponsor-review attachments such as the synopsis and schedule-of-assessments appendix, but not the SPIRIT checklist/crosswalk unless separately requested.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel understands the protocol package as the IRB submission set centered on the protocol and including the SPIRIT checklist or crosswalk and site-facing appendices expected in institutional intake.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In clinical trial practice, 'protocol package' is a common shorthand and both sides routinely work with bundles of documents, so each hears a familiar phrase and fills in their own standard contents without thinking it needs unpacking.

misalignment_points.topic: Which version is the latest draft
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to reviewing the 'latest draft' this week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena is talking about sponsor master protocol version 3.2 redline circulated Friday through sponsor document control.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel is talking about version 3.1 clean uploaded Monday to the institution's shared folder for IRB preparation, which he considers newer for practical site use because it contains the latest appendix updates.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Each version is recent and legitimately current within its own workflow, and because both are speaking cooperatively about progress rather than disputing version control, the phrase 'latest draft' feels adequately precise.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both state the goal of having the protocol 'submission-ready' by next Tuesday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means ready for sponsor governance committee circulation: major legal and regulatory issues resolved, protocol text stable, and minor site-specific placeholders still acceptable.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel means ready for single-IRB submission: all required sections complete, institutional language inserted, and all uploadable attachments present with no blanks or unresolved administrative fields.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Submission readiness is a routine milestone label used across legal and research operations, and both sides are indeed aiming at an imminent submission step, so the different completion thresholds stay hidden under shared schedule pressure.

misalignment_points.topic: How SPIRIT comments will be delivered
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that SPIRIT-based comments will be 'folded into the protocol' after Elena's review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena assumes she will mark the Word document directly with tracked changes and comments tied to SPIRIT items, expecting the revised protocol file itself to carry the review history.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel assumes Elena will populate or annotate the existing issue tracker keyed to SPIRIT checklist items, which the site team will then use to update the clean protocol offline.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'folded into the protocol' sounds outcome-focused rather than method-specific, and because both methods are standard review practices, neither participant hears anything unusual enough to trigger clarification.
